evidence.title: US Q3 domestic demand remains strong; monthly core persistence offsets quarterly disinflation
evidence.facts: Q3 advance real GDP grew 3.4% at a seasonally adjusted annualised rate, versus Q2 2.2% and the attributed web survey 3.2%; the broker-model forecast was 1.4% and is not consensus. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9%, versus 4.6%, supporting genuine private demand apart from inventories, trade and government. Investment included inventory accumulation and information-processing equipment. Exports fell and imports rose; neither is described as an independent bullish vote. Gross domestic purchases prices rose 3.0% annualised, a different measure from the GDP deflator. Quarterly PCE inflation slowed to 2.1% from 5.0%, core to 2.5% from 3.3%. Separately, September monthly headline PCE rose 0.5%, 3.6% y/y; core rose 0.3%, 3.1% y/y. Monthly core matched the 0.3% web survey but exceeded the 0.2% broker forecast. August monthly core was revised from 0.2% to 0.3%. Personal income rose 0.2%, nominal spending 0.5%, real spending less than 0.1% (rounded 0.0%), real disposable income fell 0.3%, and saving rate was 3.8%. August income is now 0.3% and real spending 0.5%; original vintages remain preserved. Strong quarterly private demand and revised monthly core persistence oppose the slower quarterly inflation and softer September household real-income/spending figures. One combined package, not a count of components.
